matches.notes: Played well, felt like the deck was balanced well and that I had strong units and counters to both opponents. Super buffing my chosen Ambessa helped clear multiple units from ivern, even with Vilemaw thanks to killing a unit when attacking. Viktor wasn't much of an issue except for Cull the weak which harmed my setups and ramping pretty bad.

This was a very close game with The Grand Plaza, both opponents conquered with over 7 units so hail mary was done from both me and Ivern player to prevent the insta win on hold. This game was super close ended with all players on 7 points and Ivern winning due to a late Vilemaw being uncontested for holding. This game was hard for me due to good RNG from Viktor with counters to my Lacerate and with 2 Cull the Weak preventing me from having units and leaving me with no cards in hand towards end game.

Loads of units with assault making it hard to hold battlefields. Probably played a bit poorly to be fair but also found a surplus of units the last round with no spells and therefore lack of removal, buffing and setup. Felt like I had loads of cheap options,  but not much to help me take control of the game and bounce back from early missplays or being countered.
Felt in control the whole game and got a really good run with the new deck. Felt in control the whole game and was able to both conquer and deal with his build up of units alright.
Played against a newbie, felt in control the whole game again with good draws, constant units and spells to help counter hsi pushes and buildups.

I was really unlucky with the draws here, and if we played bo3 it likely would have ended differently the other 2 games. Played heavy holding and I had to trade units often to prevent double points. Lucky draws for him let him kill more of my units and I was unable to come back with only spells in hand.
Taught my friend to play the game and really got to test the deck. I was easily able to build up units due to his lack of kill and removal spells. Felt in control the whole game.

I was trying it out for the first time and was really going for the yasuo strategy. It didnt work and I got run over and never really got my footing. Some spells and gear on his side killed my early build up of units.

I played for the first time into Leblanc. He had so many units with deathknell tags and played Karthus as well so constantly had great drawing and channeling. First round was kind of easy, then the second very close, and due to only drawing units and no useful spells last game I was on the backfoot the whole time. Felt like I had to use loads of resources to prevent him from getting infinite cards and then I would lose. Also the constant pressure of hidden blade and cull the weak was immense

Pretty standard rumble deck, felt in control most of the time and was able t use Rengar units well. Both rounds ended 8-7 but to be honest I felt ahead at all times. Definitely some clunky drawing at certain points. Feels like there are heaps of weaker units that dont do much once early game is done.

Super clunky draws, pure units almost no spells and once I had them I was defied anyways. Both rounds the yasuo got super good early game, double conquering anhd being at 3 or 4 points by turn 3 pretty confidently. Didnt have many asnwers early and took a while to build up. Clunky draws for sure.

First time playing it. Game 1 lost to my own misplay; game 2 was unlucky. Felt chill and in control for most of both games. Logged on 23 Sep; played with the list from before the Keeper of Law swap and the new sideboard.
Pretty easy; he definitely had poor card draw. Felt in control all the time.

Horrible, felt unwinnable at all times. He kept pumping out gear and Sand Soldiers, and in one game spent about 6 Power in 2 turns and I still could not get the upper hand. Could never take control of the game.
Early game was back and forth and I was losing out, but by midgame he was out of gas while I was healthy on cards and energy, so it became easy.
Pretty easy; it was not a very optimal Rumble deck.

gameplans.body: {"schema":"forge.gameplan/1","winPlan":[{"text":"Survive the early back-and-forth; by midgame I'm healthy on cards and energy and they're out of gas.","voice":"ours"},{"text":"Spell-slinger: the Legend's rune only pays for spells. Minimum viable unit count, maximum burn.","voice":"guide"},{"text":"Brynhir ×3 in the main: when it lands, opponents can't play cards that turn.","voice":"ours"}],"mulligan":[{"text":"No 4-card opening is dead by turn 3 in 10,000 simulated hands. [Predict] makes real openings better than that, so treat it as a floor.","voice":"forge"}],"battlefields":[{"cardId":"sfd-216-221","why":"Units can't be played there, which stops Ambush and units dropped straight in. They have to walk in, and your spells get a turn to answer.","voice":"draft"},{"cardId":"unl-212-219","why":"Deals 1 to each unit there at the start of every turn. Pick it against tokens.","voice":"draft"},{"cardId":"ven-158-166","why":"Players ignore [Deflect] when targeting there. Pick it against Deflect-heavy decks.","voice":"draft"}],"matchups":[{"id":"ks-azir","legendCardId":"sfd-197-221","archetype":"Equipment + tokens","battlefield":{"cardId":"unl-212-219","why":"1 to every unit there each turn, plus one Bellows Breath, kills a 2-Might Sand Soldier.","voice":"draft"},"bringIn":[{"cardId":"ogn-022-298","quantity":2},{"cardId":"ogs-002-024","quantity":2},{"cardId":"ven-003-166","quantity":1}],"takeOut":[{"cardId":"unl-063-219","quantity":2},{"cardId":"ogn-095-298","quantity":2},{"cardId":"ogn-096-298","quantity":1}],"watchFor":[{"text":"Lost 0-2 on 22 Sep. Felt unwinnable: he kept pumping gear and Sand Soldiers, and even spending ~6 Power in 2 turns didn't let me take control.","voice":"ours"},{"text":"His Legend only makes a Sand Soldier on a turn he played an Equipment. Gear removal switches the engine off.","voice":"guide"}],"playAround":[{"text":"Every main-deck answer trades one card for one token. Only answers that hit the whole board or the gear win this.","voice":"draft"},{"text":"Hold Thermo Beam until several pieces of equipment are down; Firestorm the battlefield where the soldiers stack.","voice":"draft"}]},{"id":"ks-ornn","legendCardId":"sfd-189-221","bringIn":[],"takeOut":[],"watchFor":[{"text":"Won 2-0 on 22 Sep. Pretty easy; he had poor card draw, and I felt in control all the time.","voice":"ours"},{"text":"Rabadon's Deathcrown gives +3 bonus damage to all his spells and abilities. It is his best piece by a distance.","voice":"guide"}],"playAround":[{"text":"Thermo Beam is the obvious side-in if his gear gets going. You won without it.","voice":"draft"}]},{"id":"ks-fiora","legendCardId":"sfd-205-221","bringIn":[],"takeOut":[],"watchFor":[{"text":"Won 2-0 on 22 Sep. Early game was back and forth and I lost ground; by midgame he was out of gas.","voice":"ours"}],"playAround":[{"text":"Don't spend removal for tempo early. Your edge is cards and energy in the midgame.","voice":"draft"}]},{"id":"ks-rumble","legendCardId":"sfd-181-221","bringIn":[],"takeOut":[],"watchFor":[{"text":"Won 2-0 on 22 Sep, against a list that wasn't very optimal, so it says little.","voice":"ours"},{"text":"His Legend gives his Mechs Shield, and Ferrous Forerunner leaves two Mechs behind when it dies.","voice":"guide"}],"playAround":[]}],"weaknesses":[{"id":"ks-sweep","threat":"A single \"deal 4 to all\" clears 14 of your 21 bodies.","playAround":"Do not over-commit once you are ahead on points. Hold back enough that a sweep costs you the board, not the game.","voice":"forge"},{"id":"ks-counter","threat":"No counterspell against bombs, recursion or ambush threats.","playAround":"Brynhir shuts them out for the turn it lands. Time Warp and Progress Day come in for long games.","voice":"draft"}]}

{"schema":"forge.gameplan/1","winPlan":[{"text":"Control, not hold: stay in control and play at my own pace. Holding a battlefield is a means, never the objective.","voice":"ours"},{"text":"The Legend's Recruit is the engine, every turn. Judge each card by what it turns a 1-Might Recruit into.","voice":"ours"},{"text":"Gold gear tokens are the rune ramp. Wages of Pain, Deadly Flourish, Honest Broker and Blood Money hand back the runes that Cull the Weak, Hidden Blade and Imperial Decree spend.","voice":"ours"}],"mulligan":[{"text":"Every 4-card opening can act by turn 3 (0 of 10,000 simulated hands had one card or fewer castable). Mulligan for the mix of answers and bodies, not for the curve.","voice":"forge"}],"battlefields":[{"cardId":"ogn-296-298","why":"Spells and abilities that affect units there deal 1 bonus damage. Bellows Breath, Wages of Pain, Crescent Strike and Singularity all get better.","voice":"draft"},{"cardId":"sfd-220-221","why":"Conquering it makes a Gold token for 1 energy, which is more rune ramp.","voice":"draft"},{"cardId":"unl-210-219","why":"A unit defending there alone gets -2 Might. Your Recruits go wide, so it mostly punishes their lone blockers.","voice":"draft"}],"matchups":[{"id":"vk-swarm","archetype":"Swarm / go-wide","battlefield":{"cardId":"ogn-296-298","why":"Crescent Strike becomes 5 to one unit and 2 to every other unit there.","voice":"draft"},"bringIn":[{"cardId":"unl-072-219","quantity":2}],"takeOut":[{"cardId":"ogn-213-298","quantity":2}],"watchFor":[{"text":"A single \"deal 2 to all\" clears 7 of your 12 bodies, so they can sweep you as easily as you sweep them.","voice":"forge"}],"playAround":[{"text":"Hidden Blade goes out because it trades one card for one token and draws them 2 cards.","voice":"draft"}]},{"id":"vk-big","archetype":"Big units","bringIn":[{"cardId":"ogn-229-298","quantity":2}],"takeOut":[{"cardId":"sfd-162-221","quantity":2}],"watchFor":[],"playAround":[{"text":"Vengeance kills anything anywhere; Blood Money cannot touch a unit above 2 Might.","voice":"draft"}]},{"id":"vk-spells","archetype":"Spell-heavy","bringIn":[{"cardId":"ven-132-166","quantity":2}],"takeOut":[{"cardId":"ogn-220-298","quantity":2}],"watchFor":[{"text":"Mind/Order has no counterspell at all. Every counter in the format needs Calm, Chaos or Body.","voice":"forge"}],"playAround":[{"text":"Name their best spell with Fallen Feline, and put Feline on a battlefield you can keep it on. The lock only holds while it is at a battlefield.","voice":"draft"}]},{"id":"vk-ornn","legendCardId":"sfd-189-221","archetype":"Gear","bringIn":[{"cardId":"sfd-160-221","quantity":2}],"takeOut":[{"cardId":"sfd-162-221","quantity":2}],"watchFor":[{"text":"Lost 0-2 on 22 Sep: game 1 to my own misplay, game 2 unlucky. Felt chill and in control for most of both.","voice":"ours"},{"text":"Rabadon's Deathcrown gives +3 bonus damage to all his spells and abilities. It is his best piece by a distance.","voice":"guide"}],"playAround":[{"text":"Zaun Punk kills one of your own Gold tokens to destroy his gear. The deck already makes the tokens it needs.","voice":"draft"}]},{"id":"vk-aggro","archetype":"Aggro","bringIn":[{"cardId":"unl-159-219","quantity":2}],"takeOut":[{"cardId":"ogn-116-298","quantity":2}],"watchFor":[],"playAround":[{"text":"Soul Harvest kills a unit with 3 Might or less for 2 energy, early, when it matters. A 7-drop is too slow here.","voice":"draft"}]}],"weaknesses":[{"id":"vk-sweep","threat":"A single \"deal 2 to all\" clears 7 of your 12 bodies.","playAround":"Do not over-commit once you are ahead on points. Hold back enough that a sweep costs you the board, not the game.","voice":"forge"},{"id":"vk-counter","threat":"No counterspell. Mind/Order cannot run one.","playAround":"Fallen Feline names their key spell. Otherwise accept it, and sequence so their best spell lands into a board that can absorb it.","voice":"draft"}]}
